lens.name: silent-failures
lens.focus: Error handling and fallbacks. List every catch, .catch, default-on-error, optional chaining or ?? fallback, retry, timeout and early return that the change adds or touches. For each, ask: which unexpected errors could it hide; did the request or spec ask for this fallback; should the failure propagate or fail closed instead; is a retry limited to transient failures, bounded by one deadline, and does it keep the original failure and its classification; does every pending or in-flight state end on every path. A failed security, isolation or inspection check that ends in silent success or an unchecked path is a blocker.

lens.name: test-gaps
lens.focus: Tests. For each new or changed behaviour, find the test that would fail if that behaviour regressed, and say so when none exists. Flag tests that assert the defect they should catch, compare the code with itself, mock away the logic under test, pass for the wrong reason (invalid fixture, swallowed error, early return, wrong file), or were weakened, skipped or special-cased to pass. Name the missing or broken test case precisely. A test gap that hides a real defect in the change is at least major; report the underlying defect itself as its own finding.

lens.name: trust-boundaries
lens.focus: Secrets, untrusted input and isolation. Trace every credential, token, private value and untrusted input (issue or PR text, gate or test output, model output, configuration or scripts from the change) from its source to every sink: logs, events, errors, PR comments, commit metadata, branch names, model prompts, files and network. Check that redaction happens after decoding and before truncation, on error and retry paths as well as the normal one. Check sandbox profiles, deny lists and allowlists for path aliases, symlinks, files versus directories, environment variables and child processes. Anything that steers the factory must come from the base commit, never the change. When isolation or a check cannot be confirmed, the code must refuse with a clear reason, never fall back silently.

Verifier: 6 candidates, 6 checked, 1 refuted.

findings.title: An excluded queued trial aborts the entire evaluation
findings.detail: `toTarget` now throws for an excluded model, but this call occurs before the trial's error handler. If a queued trial's model becomes excluded before the trial starts, the exception escapes the worker and fails the whole eval, interrupting unrelated queued or running trials instead of recording the affected trial's failure.
findings.suggestion: Handle the origin exclusion inside the trial's error boundary and record the affected trial with the exclusion reason, allowing unrelated trials to continue.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval contains several models or cases; while one trial is waiting behind another, its runtime model is patched from US to CN under a CN exclusion. When that trial starts, the eval fails and remaining trials are interrupted.

findings.detail: The new condition applies a stricter definition of text than Git's diff classification. It flags executable text containing non-UTF-8 bytes or control characters, and flags executable text under a media extension regardless of its contents. It also newly blocks a non-UTF-8 text file when an edit removes its executable bit: the old condition did not flag a mode change accompanied by a content change. These paths can be shown as text in the diff but are reported as binary content.

findings.title: Draft deferrals never resume when GitHub polling is disabled
findings.detail: Skipped draft triggers are no longer returned by pendingConflictTriggers, and the only code that reactivates them is in the GitHub poller. The supported github.poll = false configuration does not start that poller, so a land-triggered conflict deferred while a PR is a draft remains skipped permanently, even after the PR becomes ready or the daemon restarts.
findings.suggestion: Provide a change-observation path for installations with polling disabled, or preserve a bounded fallback for that configuration.
findings.failure_scenario: Set github.poll = false, create a land conflict trigger while the PR is a draft, then mark the PR ready on the same head. Subsequent conflict processing never sees the skipped trigger and no round starts.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/index.ts:38-45 starts `startGitHubPoller` only when `factory.cfg.githubPoll` is true. src/db/store.ts:1114 selects conflict triggers only `WHERE state = 'pending'`, excluding draft deferrals. The only caller of `recheckDraftConflictTriggers` is src/integrations/github-poller.ts:373-374: `store.recheckDraftConflictTriggers(pr.url, snap)`. src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:14 processes only `store.pendingConflictTriggers()`.
verification.trigger: With github.poll=false, a land conflict trigger skipped as 'PR is draft' remains skipped after the PR becomes ready on the same head. Subsequent conflict processing cannot select it, so its round never starts.

candidates.title: A head change can be missed while a draft lookup is in flight
candidates.detail: The request says to recheck a draft deferral when the poller observes “a new head.” This guard compares the snapshot only with the poller's previous snapshot. If the poller saves the new head before an in-flight live lookup marks an older-head trigger as draft, subsequent polls see the same head and never call recheckDraftConflictTriggers, even though that method would detect the mismatch against the trigger's observed SHA. The deferred trigger remains stale until another qualifying change occurs.
candidates.suggestion: Check deferred triggers against each observed snapshot, or otherwise make recording the deferral and observing the head change race-safe.
candidates.failure_scenario: A trigger for head A starts a live lookup. While it is awaiting GitHub, the poller observes and saves draft head B. The lookup then returns a draft result and marks the A trigger skipped. Later polls continue to observe draft head B, so the skipped trigger is never rechecked for the A-to-B head change.

The only caller of `recheckDraftConflictTriggers` is src/integrations/github-poller.ts:373-374: `store.recheckDraftConflictTriggers(pr.url, snap)`. src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:14 processes only `store.pendingConflictTriggers()`.

verdicts.evidence: src/integrations/github-poller.ts:375-376 processes pending triggers during the observation: `for (const trigger of store.pendingConflictTriggers()) { if (trigger.prUrl === pr.url) store.startConflictTrigger(trigger.id, snap, now()); }`. Thus the pending A trigger is checked against draft B immediately. src/db/store.ts:1177-1178 defers it again: `seen.isDraft ? "PR is draft"`. The late lookup cannot overwrite this: src/db/store.ts:1143-1144 re-reads pending triggers and returns when absent: `const trigger = this.pendingConflictTriggers().find((t) => t.id === id); if (!trigger || trigger.nextAttemptAt > now) return null;`.
verdicts.trigger: While a live lookup is awaiting GitHub, the poller observes draft head B. It checks the pending trigger against B and defers it because B remains draft; the late lookup becomes a no-op. The head change is therefore checked.

findings.title: A saved head change can be lost before the draft deferral is rechecked
findings.detail: The poller saves the new snapshot before reactivating draft triggers, and uses the saved snapshot on the next pass to decide whether the head changed. If the process stops between those operations, the next pass sees the same head and an open draft, so it never rechecks the deferred trigger. The same ordering can occur when a live lookup finishes after the poller has saved the newer head and marks the trigger as draft. The trigger remains skipped despite the poller having observed a new head.
findings.suggestion: Make recording the observation and reactivating eligible draft triggers durable together, or compare each deferred trigger's recorded head with the current observation on every poll.
findings.failure_scenario: A trigger is skipped as draft at head A. The poller observes draft head B and saves it, then the daemon restarts before rechecking triggers. Subsequent observations of draft head B do not reactivate the trigger.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/github-poller.ts:372-374 saves first: `save(unknown ? (prev?.nudged ?? null) : null);` then separately checks `if (!same || snap.isDraft === false || snap.state !== "OPEN") store.recheckDraftConflictTriggers(pr.url, snap);`. `same` is `prev?.headRefOid === head` (line 345). src/db/store.ts:2661-2675 commits the saved observation in its own transaction. src/db/store.ts:1114 reads only triggers `WHERE state = 'pending'`.

After restart, unchanged open draft B makes the recheck condition false. This is a very narrow synchronous crash window; becoming ready or closing still reactivates it.

findings.failure_scenario: With `[github] poll = false`, a land conflict trigger encounters a draft PR and is marked skipped. The PR later becomes ready on the same head, but no conflict round starts because neither the queue nor any poller reactivates the trigger.

verification.trigger: With `[github] poll = false`, a land conflict trigger is deferred while its PR is draft. Making the PR ready on the same head leaves that trigger skipped indefinitely, so no conflict round starts automatically.

findings.title: An excluded queued trial aborts the entire evaluation
findings.detail: `toTarget` now throws for an excluded model, but this call occurs before the trial's error handler. If a queued trial's model becomes excluded before the trial starts, the exception escapes the worker and fails the whole eval, interrupting unrelated queued or running trials instead of recording the affected trial's failure.
findings.suggestion: Handle the origin exclusion inside the trial's error boundary and record the affected trial with the exclusion reason, allowing unrelated trials to continue.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval contains several models or cases; while one trial is waiting behind another, its runtime model is patched from US to CN under a CN exclusion. When that trial starts, the eval fails and remaining trials are interrupted.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:592 reads the current model: `const model = router.model(trial.modelId)`. Line 617 calls `router.toTarget(model, effort ?? null)` before the `try` at line 625. src/router/router.ts:168 throws on exclusion: `if (origin) throw new Error(...)`. The worker catches this at src/evals/runner.ts:499–502 with `failed = true; throw error`; execution then calls `store.interruptEval(run.id, (error as Error).message, "failed")` at line 524. src/db/store.ts:554–557 marks remaining queued/running trials `skipped`. Runtime origin edits are possible through src/router/runtime-catalog.ts:83–104, which merges the patch and applies the updated model.
verification.trigger: With CN excluded, submit several trials sharing a provider. While an earlier trial runs, patch a later trial's runtime model from US to CN. When that queued trial starts, target construction escapes its error handler, fails the eval and skips unfinished trials. This requires an unusual catalog edit during an active eval.

findings.title: Verifier failure can omit the exclusion that exhausted the choices
findings.detail: The exclusion reason is propagated only when every listed verifier is excluded. If an allowed verifier remains but is ineligible because it raised the candidate, `pickVerifier` throws a different error that omits the excluded alternative. The invocation therefore fails without the required origin exclusion reason.
findings.suggestion: Include collected exclusion reasons when verifier selection fails after filtering, and log excluded verifier choices.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier list contains an allowed model that raised the candidate and a CN model excluded by configuration. No verifier can be selected, but the error reports only that the allowed model raised the candidate.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1341–1349 removes excluded targets with `exclusions.push(`${targetId}: ${reason}`); return [];`, but reports those reasons only when `!listed.length && exclusions.length`. Otherwise it calls `pickVerifier(listed, avoidVendors, avoidModels, identity)`. src/pipeline/review.ts:325–328 throws `NoCapacityError(`verifier ${targets.map((t) => t.modelId).join(", ")} raised a candidate it would check`)` when no remaining target is independent.
verification.trigger: With CN excluded, the verifier list contains an excluded CN model and an allowed model that raised the candidate. The allowed model keeps `listed` nonempty, so selection fails with only the raised-candidate message, omitting the origin exclusion.

findings.title: Cover a catalog origin change while a production invocation is waiting
findings.detail: The new queued-origin tests exercise eval and chat calls, but no test covers a normal pipeline invocation whose selected runtime model becomes excluded while it waits for a provider slot or before dispatch. The existing pipeline race tests change routing cells or provider preference, so they would not catch a regression in catalog-driven routing invalidation.
findings.suggestion: Add a fake-harness pipeline test that selects an allowed runtime model, blocks it before dispatch, patches its origin to an excluded value, and verifies that it is never invoked and the exclusion reason is reported.
findings.failure_scenario: A runtime model is changed from US to CN while a production run is queued. If catalog edits stop invalidating the routing revision, the stale target can be dispatched despite the configured CN exclusion without an existing test failing.

verification.evidence: test/pipeline.test.ts:9484-9498 tests queued production edits with `test.each(["cell", "prefer"])`, calling only `runtime.setCell(...)` or `runtime.setPrefer(...)`; it does not exercise catalog edits. The origin test at test/pipeline.test.ts:8046-8049 sets origins before constructing the router. Production currently relies on src/router/router.ts:76-79: `setModels(...) { ... this.invalidateRouting(); }` and src/pipeline/context.ts:582-586: `if (revision.aborted) { release?.(); ... continue; }`. Queued origin-change tests in test/evals-runner.test.ts:22-46 exercise evals, whose separate guard is `router.assertOriginEligible(to.target.modelId)` (src/evals/runner.ts:898).
verification.trigger: Removing catalog-edit routing invalidation could let a queued production invocation dispatch a previously selected model after its origin changes from US to excluded CN, without the existing production tests detecting that regression. This is a coverage gap; current invalidation prevents the bypass.

findings.title: Verifier exclusions are omitted from the run log
findings.detail: The request says the skip reason in the run log reads `origin excluded (<origin>; baseOrigin=<baseOrigin>)`. This verifier-selection path removes excluded alternatives before calling the router, but logs their reasons only when every listed target is excluded. When an allowed verifier remains, the exclusion is invisible in the run log.
findings.suggestion: Record the excluded verifier alternatives and their reasons when filtering them, including when another verifier is selected.
findings.failure_scenario: A review system lists one CN verifier and one US verifier with CN excluded; the US verifier runs, but the run log does not explain that the CN verifier was skipped.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1337–1350 collects exclusions locally, removes those targets, and passes only the selected allowed target through `call(request, { ...constraints, only }, undefined)`, without logging `exclusions`. src/router/router.ts:386–387 handles that constraint with `consider([c.only])`. src/pipeline/context.ts:659–662 logs the invocation with `skipped: decision.skipped`, which therefore contains no entry for the previously removed CN verifier.
verification.trigger: A verifier list contains an excluded CN model and an eligible US model. The US verifier runs, but the CN exclusion collected before routing never reaches the run log.

findings.title: Verifier exhaustion can hide the origin exclusion reason
findings.detail: The request says that when exclusions leave no candidate, the invocation fails with the origin exclusion reason. This check reports exclusions only if the filtered list is empty. If the remaining allowed targets are ineligible because they raised the finding, `pickVerifier` throws a different error that omits the excluded alternatives and their reasons.
findings.suggestion: Include the collected exclusion reasons when verifier selection fails after applying the independence constraints.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier list contains an excluded CN model and an allowed US model, and the US model raised the candidate being verified. Selection fails with only the raised-candidate message, despite the CN exclusion preventing the other choice.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1341–1349 filters excluded targets into `exclusions`, throws their reasons only for `!listed.length`, then calls `pickVerifier` with the remaining targets. src/pipeline/review.ts:321–328 rejects targets whose identity appears in `avoidModels` and throws only `verifier ... raised a candidate it would check`; it receives no exclusion reasons.

findings.detail: The new condition applies a stricter definition of text than Git's diff classification. It flags executable text containing non-UTF-8 bytes or control characters, and flags executable text under a media extension regardless of its contents. It also newly blocks a non-UTF-8 text file when an edit removes its executable bit: the old condition did not flag a mode change accompanied by a content change. These paths can be shown as text in the diff but are reported as binary content.

findings.title: Draft deferrals never resume when GitHub polling is disabled
findings.detail: Skipped draft triggers are no longer returned by pendingConflictTriggers, and the only code that reactivates them is in the GitHub poller. The supported github.poll = false configuration does not start that poller, so a land-triggered conflict deferred while a PR is a draft remains skipped permanently, even after the PR becomes ready or the daemon restarts.
findings.suggestion: Provide a change-observation path for installations with polling disabled, or preserve a bounded fallback for that configuration.
findings.failure_scenario: Set github.poll = false, create a land conflict trigger while the PR is a draft, then mark the PR ready on the same head. Subsequent conflict processing never sees the skipped trigger and no round starts.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/index.ts:38–45 starts the poller only when `factory.cfg.githubPoll` is true, otherwise using `() => {}`. src/land/queue.ts:685–686 records a conflict trigger with `if (conflict) this.store.recordConflictTrigger(...)`, and :303 invokes `processConflictTriggers`. src/db/store.ts:1177–1191 classifies a draft as `"PR is draft"` and persists `state = 'skipped'`. src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:14 processes only `store.pendingConflictTriggers()`, whose query at src/db/store.ts:1114 now selects only `WHERE state = 'pending'`. The sole caller of `recheckDraftConflictTriggers` is the disabled poller (src/integrations/github-poller.ts:373–374).
verification.trigger: With the supported but nondefault `github.poll = false` configuration, a land conflict trigger deferred while its PR is draft remains skipped after the PR becomes ready on the same head. Later conflict processing, including daemon startup, cannot select it, so its conflict round never starts automatically.

candidates.detail: The request says to recheck a draft deferral when the poller observes “a new head.” This guard compares the snapshot only with the poller's previous snapshot. If the poller saves the new head before an in-flight live lookup marks an older-head trigger as draft, subsequent polls see the same head and never call recheckDraftConflictTriggers, even though that method would detect the mismatch against the trigger's observed SHA. The deferred trigger remains stale until another qualifying change occurs.

The lookup then returns a draft result and marks the A trigger skipped. Later polls continue to observe draft head B, so the skipped trigger is never rechecked for the A-to-B head change.

verdicts.evidence: The poller's own lookup and observation are serial: src/integrations/github-poller.ts:476 awaits `processConflictTriggers(...)` before :484 executes `await observe(repo, prs)`. For a concurrent land-queue lookup, the observation synchronously processes pending triggers at :375–376: `for (const trigger of store.pendingConflictTriggers()) { if (trigger.prUrl === pr.url) store.startConflictTrigger(trigger.id, snap, now()); }`. Draft B therefore already skips the pending A trigger. A late lookup cannot overwrite it: src/db/store.ts:1143–1144 re-reads pending state with `const trigger = this.pendingConflictTriggers().find((t) => t.id === id); if (!trigger || trigger.nextAttemptAt > now) return null;`.

findings.title: A saved head change can be lost before the draft deferral is rechecked
findings.detail: The poller saves the new snapshot before reactivating draft triggers, and uses the saved snapshot on the next pass to decide whether the head changed.
